name: Calculating the Average of the Values in the Array
description: Construct a program that calculates the average of all the values in an array. The program should handle arrays with arbitrary number of values (including an empty array).

comments.content: We define array lst to hold the specified numbers. We initialize the array by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in braces { }.
We need variable total to maintain a running total, which means the sum of the values in the array. Of course, the total should be initialized with 0.

We use a for loop to iterate over the array elements and add each element to the running total. We can do this by using for–each statement that visits each element in the array. This for loop assigns the name x to each of the items in the array in turn, from left to right, and then the statement in the loop body will be executed for each value.

We need to add each value in the array to the running total that is stored in variable total. So, in each iteration, we add the array element that we visited to the variable total and store the result back into the variable total.
The += operator adds the value of variable x to the value of the variable total and the result is stored in the variable total. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement total = total + x.

We need the if statement to avoid a divide-by-zero error. This occurs if the array has no values.

To determine if the divide-by-zero error would occur, we need to test if the number of values in the array is equal to zero.
If the number of values in the array is equal to zero, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
lst.length returns the number of the values in the array.
This statement prints the given text to the default standard output stream. Each printed value is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

If the above if test fails (i.e., when the number of values in the array is different from zero), we could calculate the average by dividing the sum of array values by the number of values in the array.

We need to calculate the average by dividing the sum of the values in the array by the number of the values in the array. Notice that both variables in the division are int and dividing an int by an int results in an int. Since we want to keep the fractional part, we need to cast one of the operands to a floating point data type like double.

When floating point value total is divided by an integer value returned from the expression lst.length, the value returned by lst.length is promoted to a floating point value automatically, before the division takes place, producing a floating point result.
lst.length returns the number of the elements in the array.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the average of all values in the array.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and value of the variable.
